theory.intro: A **composite solid** is built from simple solids. Find its volume by splitting it into parts you know, working out each part's volume, then adding or subtracting them.
facts: Split the solid into named simple parts and find each part's volume with its own formula.
Cone $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h$; cylinder $V = \pi r^{2}h$; sphere $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}$; hemisphere $V = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^{3}$; pyramid $V = \frac{1}{3}Ah$.
Two hemispheres of the same radius together make one whole sphere.
Keep each part's volume **unrounded** and round only the final total, so no rounding error builds up.
For capacity, convert the total: $1$ cm³ $= 1$ mL, $1000$ cm³ $= 1$ L, $1$ m³ $= 1000$ L.
steps: Split the composite solid into simple solids
Find the volume of each simple solid

workedExamples.solution_text:
Add the cylinder and cone volumes. Keep exact values until the final rounding.

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{cylinder}}&=\pi r^2h\\&=\pi(2)^2(6)\\&=24\pi\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{cone}}&=\frac13\pi r^2h\\&=\frac13\pi(2)^2(3)\\&=4\pi\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{total}}&=24\pi+4\pi\\&=28\pi\\&\approx87.96\text{ m}^3\\&\approx88.0\text{ m}^3\quad\text{(1 d.p.)}\end{align*}$

Add the cone and hemisphere volumes.

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{cone}}&=\frac13\pi r^2h\\&=\frac13\pi(3)^2(9)\\&=27\pi\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{hemisphere}}&=\frac12\times\frac43\pi r^3\\&=\frac12\times\frac43\pi(3)^3\\&=18\pi\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{total}}&=27\pi+18\pi\\&=45\pi\\&\approx141.37\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$

Add the cylinder and hemisphere volumes.

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{cylinder}}&=\pi r^2h\\&=\pi(3)^2(7)\\&=63\pi\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{hemisphere}}&=\frac12\times\frac43\pi r^3\\&=\frac12\times\frac43\pi(3)^3\\&=18\pi\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{total}}&=63\pi+18\pi\\&=81\pi\\&\approx254.5\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$

The two hemispheres make one sphere.

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{cylinder}}&=\pi r^2h\\&=\pi(4)^2(8)\\&=128\pi\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{two hemispheres}}&=\frac43\pi r^3\\&=\frac43\pi(4)^3\\&=\frac{256\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{total}}&=128\pi+\frac{256\pi}{3}\\&=\frac{640\pi}{3}\\&\approx670.2\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$

The pyramid's perpendicular height is $11-4=7$ m.

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{prism}}&=Ah\\&=(6\times6)(4)\\&=144\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{pyramid}}&=\frac13Ah\\&=\frac13(6\times6)(7)\\&=84\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{total}}&=144+84\\&=228\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$

Subtract the scoop's volume, then compare the remaining volume with the original cube.

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{cube}}&=10^3\\&=1000\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}V_{\text{scoop}}&=\frac12\times\frac43\pi r^3\\&=\frac12\times\frac43\pi(5)^3\\&=\frac{250\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$

$V_{\text{remaining}}=1000-\frac{250\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^3$

$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage remaining}&=\frac{1000-\frac{250\pi}{3}}{1000}\times100\%\\&\approx73.82\%\\&\approx74\%\quad\text{(nearest whole percentage)}\end{align*}$

foundation.question_text:
Two square-based pyramids are joined along their matching bases. Each base has side length $3$ cm. The perpendicular heights of the pyramids are $5$ cm and $4$ cm.
Find the total volume in cm³, correct to $2$ decimal places.

development.question_text:
A cone sits exactly inside a cylinder. Both have radius $5$ cm and perpendicular height $12$ cm.
What fraction of the volume of the cylinder is the cone?

An ice-cream is a cone of radius $2.5$ cm and height $10$ cm, topped with a hemisphere of the same radius.
Find its total volume in cm³, correct to $2$ decimal places.

A capsule-shaped tank is a cylinder of radius $0.5$ m and height $2$ m with a hemisphere on each end (together a full sphere).
Find its volume in m³, correct to $1$ decimal place.

A hemispherical scoop of radius $4$ cm is taken out of a cubic tub with edge length $8$ cm. The circular opening fits exactly across the top of the cube.
Find the volume that remains as a percentage of the cube's volume, rounded to the nearest whole percentage.

mastery.question_text:
A square-based pyramid sits exactly on top of a cube to form a solid.
The cube has an edge of $5$ m and the pyramid has a perpendicular height of $9$ m. Find the total volume of the solid in m³.

Two square-based pyramids are joined along their matching bases. Each base has side length $3$ cm. Their perpendicular heights are $7$ cm and $11$ cm.
Find the total volume in cm³, correct to $2$ decimal places.
A grain silo is a cylinder of radius $2$ m and height $5$ m, topped by a cone of the same radius and height $1.5$ m. Find its total volume in m³, correct to $1$ decimal place.
